function: Externalises three of the five 88-level lookup tables declared in the
frozen COBOL copybook app/cpy/CSLKPCDY.cpy as classpath reference data.
The three tables are the North American Numbering Plan area-code sets used
to validate a customer telephone area code.

sourceCopybookRole: The COBOL corpus under app/ is frozen and read-only. It is simultaneously
the parity oracle, the field-contract source and the traceability anchor
for this migration, so it is never edited, moved or reformatted.
parentDataItemNote: All three condition names below are 88-level condition names on this one
three-character parent item. They are three distinct tables, not one table
transcription: Every value is transcribed verbatim from the frozen COBOL corpus, in source
order, with no value added, removed, sorted, deduplicated, re-cased or
reformatted. A value that differs from the copybook is a parity break, not
a correction: the copybook is the sole authority.
extractionMethod: Comment-skipping literal extraction: within each inclusive line range, a
line whose first non-blank character is '*' is a COBOL comment and is
skipped; every remaining single-quoted literal is collected in source
order. Fixed-column slicing is unsafe here because the continuation-line
indentation is not uniform, so it is not used.
statementTerminator: Each table's final source line ends '999'. or '989'. - the trailing period
closes the COBOL statement and is not part of the value.
interiorComment: 'Easily recognizable codes begin here.' inside the range of
VALID-PHONE-AREA-CODE. It is skipped and contributes no value.
networkSources: None. This resource is produced only from the frozen copybook. No value is
fetched, refreshed or reconciled over the network at build time or run
time, and this resource performs no outbound access of any kind.

citedText: North America Phone area codes List obtained from North America
usage: Historical provenance only. This address records where the legacy authors
originally sourced the list. It is never fetched and the live registry is
never used to add, remove or correct a value, because that would break
parity with the system of record.

summary: The complete set of area codes accepted by the legacy validation.
Deliberately NOT in ascending order: it is the general-purpose run
followed by the easily-recognisable run, so index 409 ('989') is
immediately followed by index 410 ('200'). That ordering is source
The general-purpose area codes. Ascending, no duplicates.
The easily recognisable area codes. Ascending, no duplicates.
Enumerated literally rather than generated from any pattern.

invariants: Element counts are exactly 490, 410 and 80; any other count is a Blocker.
Every element is a JSON string of exactly three ASCII digits - never a
number, because the source field is PIC XXX character data.
No element is null, empty, whitespace-padded or duplicated within its array.
The three tables are independent and must never be merged, unioned or
flattened into one list, and none may be dropped or derived from the
others even though that concatenation identity holds.

metadataHandling: This _metadata member is documentation, NOT data. The consuming service
ignores it explicitly and deliberately by its well-known name; it is never
bound as a lookup table and never participates in validation.
bindingContract: Read as UTF-8 from the classpath and bound with plain, explicitly typed
Jackson binding to string collections. No polymorphic type handling and no
default typing are used or required, and this resource carries no type
hint of any kind, so it cannot drive insecure deserialisation.
exposure: Loaded once at startup into immutable collections, so no caller can mutate

whatItDoes: Supplies the three North American Numbering Plan area-code tables that the
VALID-GENERAL-PURP-CODE and VALID-EASY-RECOG-AREA-CODE expressed in COBOL.
A membership test against the appropriate table replaces evaluating the
howToBuildAndTest: No build step: this is a static classpath resource copied verbatim into
target/classes by the standard resources phase, with no property filtering.
Build with './mvnw -B clean compile' and run the unit suite with
'./mvnw -B clean test'. The assertions for this resource live under
src/test/java/com/cardemo/unit/ and cover the three element counts, the
first and last value of each table, interior index checkpoints, the
disjointness of the two subsets and the concatenation identity.
configurationAndDefaults: No configuration and no defaults: the content is fixed reference data and
there is no property, profile or environment variable that alters it.
The resource path itself is the only contract with the consumer.
Encoding is UTF-8 with LF line endings and two-space indentation, per the
commonFailureModesAndTroubleshooting: Resource not found on the classpath: the consumer must fail fast and
loudly rather than degrade to an empty table, because an empty table
would silently reject every telephone number. Confirm the file is present
Malformed content: the consumer must wrap the parse failure with this
resource path and preserve the root cause. Re-validate the file with a
Unexpected element count: compare against the counts published in
sourceTables above. A mismatch means the resource was truncated or
edited, and it is a Blocker - re-derive it from app/cpy/CSLKPCDY.cpy.
An area code rejected that the legacy system accepted: verify the value
against the copybook line range, never against any external registry.

designRationale: These tables are data, not code. Generating them as Java constants would
add well over a thousand lines of source that no compiler check makes
safer, would make the counts hard to audit, and would put reference data
in the compilation unit. Externalising them as a classpath resource keeps
the membership exactly auditable against the copybook, keeps the counts
visible for verification, and is the justified tradeoff recorded here.
notAvailable: The semantic distinction the source intends between 'general purpose' and
'easily recognisable', beyond the proven disjoint partition of the two
sets: Not available. The copybook declares both sets but documents no rule,
and no numbering-plan documentation exists in this repository, so no
behaviour is inferred from the condition names.
A lookup latency or throughput objective: Not available. The legacy source
publishes no service level, so none is invented here; the performance gate
records a measured baseline rather than a target.
